live.offHint: No live connection – data is reloaded every 30 s

ip.title: Public IP
ip.refreshHint: Check IP and sync all records

isp.providerHint: Network (autonomous system) the address belongs to

blocklist.policyHint: Spamhaus PBL lists almost all residential connections. This is normal and only matters for your own mail server – it should send through a relay.
blocklist.refusedHint: Spamhaus does not answer queries via public resolvers (e.g. 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8). Let the container use your router's or provider's resolver.

dashboard.subtitle: Public addresses, DNS records and recent changes
dashboard.ipChangesHint: The ten most recent changes of the public addresses

records.subtitle: DNS records that should point to the public IP
records.notConfiguredHint: Set CF_API_TOKEN in deploy/.env and restart the container. Required permissions: Zone → DNS → Edit, Zone → Zone → Read.
records.logHint: Created and changed records as well as errors
records.removeHint: <name>{{name}}</name> will be removed from dnsdeck and no longer updated. The record at Cloudflare stays unchanged.

recordDialog.addHint: If the record does not exist at Cloudflare, it is created with these values. If it already exists, dnsdeck adopts proxy and TTL from Cloudflare and only changes the IP.
recordDialog.editHint: Changed proxy/TTL values are applied to Cloudflare immediately.
recordDialog.name: Name
recordDialog.proxiedHint: Orange cloud: traffic goes through Cloudflare, the TTL is then automatic.
recordDialog.enabledHint: Disabled: the record stays managed but is not changed.
recordDialog.probeHint: Requests {{url}} regularly and monitors its certificate.

tunnels.subtitle: Cloudflare Tunnels of your account
tunnels.notConfiguredHint: Set CF_API_TOKEN and CF_ACCOUNT_ID in deploy/.env and restart the container. The token additionally needs the permission Account → Cloudflare Tunnel → Read.
tunnels.empty: No tunnels found in the account.
tunnels.gaps: Gaps in the period (grey): dnsdeck or Cloudflare were unreachable

history.subtitle: DNS updates, IP changes and tunnel status changes

settings.subtitle: Intervals, IP sources and webhooks
settings.intervalsHint: Changes take effect immediately, no restart needed.
settings.ipIntervalHint: The maximum time a record points to the old IP after an IP change.
settings.tunnelIntervalHint: Determines how quickly a tunnel outage is detected.
settings.sourcesHint: The public IP is only accepted when the majority of sources agree. Enable at least {{min}}, recommended: all.
settings.notificationsHint: Title and text of all webhook messages.
settings.notifyLanguageHint: Independent of the interface language, which each browser chooses itself.
settings.probeIntervalHint: An outage is reported after two failures in a row.
settings.tlsWarnDaysHint: Remaining validity at which a certificate counts as “expiring” and is reported.

ip_change.label: IP change
ip_change.hint: The public IPv4 or IPv6 address has changed.

update_failed.label: DNS update failed
update_failed.hint: Once per new error, not on every retry.

update_recovered.label: DNS update OK again
update_recovered.hint: A previously failing record is up to date again.

blocklist_listed.label: IP on blocklist
blocklist_listed.hint: The public IPv4 was newly found on a DNS blocklist (e.g. Spamhaus) – relevant for your own mail server.

site_down.label: Unreachable
site_down.hint: A checked address stopped responding or its certificate is invalid.

site_recovered.label: Reachable again
site_recovered.hint: A previously failing address responds again.

cert_expiring.label: Certificate expiring
cert_expiring.hint: Once per certificate when the configured remaining validity is reached.

webhooks.title: Notifications (webhooks)
webhooks.subtitle: Notify any service via HTTP request – presets for ntfy, Gotify, Discord, Slack, Telegram and Home Assistant.
webhooks.noEvents: No event selected – sends test messages only
webhooks.missingEnv: Not set: {{names}} – add to deploy/.env and restart the container.
webhooks.deleteHint: “{{name}}” will be deleted and receive no more notifications. The environment variables in deploy/.env stay unchanged.
webhooks.secretsHint: Never enter secrets directly: use {{urlVar}} in URL and headers, {{bodyVar}} in the body. The values belong in deploy/.env.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.envIntro: Add to deploy/.env, then restart the container:

env.WEBHOOK_DISCORD_URL: full webhook URL from the channel settings

webhooks.bodyPlaceholder: Empty = default JSON with type, title, message, priority, time, data
webhooks.previewHint: Placeholders stay visible in the preview – values are never shown.

system.title: System
system.hint: Credentials are never shown, only whether they are set.

propagation.title: DNS propagation

status.partial: Partially propagated – some resolvers still serve the old state from their cache

propagation.expectProxied: proxied – IP hidden, only resolvability is checked
propagation.stale: Outdated – the record has changed since the check

checks.subtitle: Are your services responding, and how long are their certificates valid?
checks.empty: No checks yet. Enter an address above or turn on “Check reachability” for a record.
checks.removeRecordHint: <url>{{url}}</url> will no longer be checked. The record itself is kept.
checks.howItWorks: dnsdeck requests each address with GET and does not follow redirects. Any response below 500 counts as reachable – a login page too. Certificates are reported {{days}} days before they expire.
checks.hairpin: Checks run from inside the container. Addresses not routed through Cloudflare are sometimes unreachable from your own network although they work from outside (missing NAT loopback on the router).
